source_ref: Deposit: Al-Qerem (2024), Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.10812303, CC BY 4.0, 'Data for submission.sav' (variable labels). Paper: Al-Qerem, Jarab, Eberhardt, Alasmari, Alkaee & Alsabaa (2024), Healthcare 12(7):801, doi:10.3390/healthcare12070801 (PMC11011997), CC BY 4.0, Tables 2-3.
note: ITEM MAPPING NEEDS NO INFERENCE: data/alqerem_2024_diabetic_health_literacy.py melts the .sav columns N1,N2,N3,N5,c1,c2,C3 and only upper-cases them, and each column carries its own SPSS variable label (7/7), which is what item_text ships verbatim. The paper (Healthcare 12:801, CC BY 4.0) independently corroborates it: its Table 2 per-item counts reproduce exactly for all four N items and at unique anchor cells for the three C items (verify script). Wording differs slightly from the paper's Table 2/3 (e.g. .sav N2 'Understand the written information provided at the appointment' vs paper 'Understand the written information I receive from my healthcare provider'); the .sav labels were preferred as level 1. The paper's 8th item, 'Evaluate the accuracy of diabetes-related information I obtain', is absent from the deposit (hence no N4). LANGUAGE FALLBACK: the paper says the JDHLQ was back-translated into Arabic and administered to Jordanian patients; the deposit (single .sav, zero Arabic characters across variable and value labels) and the paper (no supplementary files, zero Arabic characters) carry no Arabic wording, so the study's English labels ship in the base fields. OPTION_TEXT IS DELIBERATELY BLANK, because the deposit's resp codes do not mean what its value labels say. The .sav value labels read 1 Never, 2 Rarely, 3 Sometimes, 4 Most of the time, 5 '' (empty), but the paper analysed a 1-4 scale, and for N1/N2/N3/N5 its Table 2 counts are reproduced exactly only by live 1->paper 1, live 2->paper 3, live 3->paper 4, live 4 and 5->paper 2 (N1 live 44/198/65/36/57 vs paper 44/93/198/65; remapped means 2.710/2.737/2.655/2.700 vs Table 3 2.71/2.74/2.66/2.70). The C items fit no clean collapse (C2 live 63/153/124/13/47 vs paper 63/155/133/49). Shipping the value labels would put 'Rarely' on a code that is the paper's third level. The paper prints no anchor wording. Rights: the JDHLQ is these authors' own instrument, first published in a CC BY 4.0 article; deposit CC BY 4.0; no restriction on the wording located.
public_note: Seven items from the Jordanian Diabetic Health Literacy Questionnaire, on understanding diabetes information and communicating about diabetes; the wording is the study's own English labels, while patients answered an Arabic version that was not published. THE RESPONSE CODES ARE NOT A CLEAN ORDERED SCALE: the paper analysed a four-point scale, but the deposited data use five codes, and for the four information items the published frequencies are only reproduced if code 2 is the paper's third level, code 3 its fourth, and codes 4 and 5 together its second, so higher resp does not mean higher literacy and no anchor labels are shown.
